correctness.rationale: On the 35 triples, the BFS and Johnson-scheme projectors give sector multiplicities 1,6,14,14 and the exact rows (1,12,18,4), (1,5,-3,-3), (1,0,-3,2), (1,-3,3,-1). On the orthocomplement of constants, the powered-distance multipliers are 5·2^p-3·3^p-3, 2-3·3^p, 3·3^p-3·2^p-1. The first two stay strictly negative, including the rational cubic bound 229/243 for the first; the third crosses zero exactly once in (0,1). The centered Gram rank follows. Polynomial distance-exponential multipliers factor to (1-x)(1-2x+3x²), (1-x)(1+3x+3x²), (1-x)(1-3x²); the last imposes x≤1/sqrt(3), giving t≥log3/2. Actual exact stdlib checker and independent pencil sign reconstruction agree; numerical root approximations are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The novel claimed information is an exact spectral-sign phase classification on the first non-Petersen odd graph: a unique negative-type exponent, a 14-dimensional endpoint rank drop, and a sharp individual positive-bandwidth distance-exponential cutoff. Inspected general finite negative-type theory, the classical Kneser ordinary-distance spectrum, and the broad Q-matrix characterization did not state the same outcomes. Publicly indexed and accessible own-history searches found no statement that implies these parameters. This is bounded, not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent specialization of the classical Johnson Eberlein coefficients may already calculate these exact thresholds.
Ordinary-distance spectral data used as inputs are established, so the novelty rests exclusively on the derived powered-distance and exponential parameter classifications.
No independent expert priority audit is performed.

value.rationale: KG(7,3) is the canonical fourth odd graph, a natural distance-transitive 35-point homogeneous metric with three nonzero distances. Its exact supremal negative-type exponent, sharp 14-dimensional loss of Euclidean embedding rank at the endpoint, and distinct distance-exponential cutoff provide a complete, motivated classification of metric embedding and covariance admissibility quantities on this standard space. These nonlinear spectral-sign invariants are not determined by a table of the ordinary distance eigenvalues without further analysis. Limited to one graph and one fully solved supercritical bandwidth slice, but a natural complete invariant and sharp phase boundary are valuable.
